properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: capabilities form a DEPENDS_ON DAG that detect_defects insists stays acyclic, and NOTHING ever asks what order it implies. reflow2 can say what is scheduled for an increment (SCHEDULED_FOR) and what is delivered (the golden thread), but not what can be started.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::topological_sort — Kahn's, deterministic (lexicographically smallest order), returns None on a cycle. Two distinct uses:
(a) A SIMPLIFICATION available today: budget.rs:312 hand-rolls Kahn's algorithm in about forty lines with a comment that says so. The foundation exports it.
(b) A NEW capability: given the capabilities scheduled for an increment, a valid build order — and the frontier of what has no unbuilt dependency, which is "what can I pick up now".

WHERE IT LANDS: BL-68 (TRL/MRL readiness gating) is about whether something is ready; this is about whether its DEPENDENCIES are ready, which is the other half of the same question. Also epoch planning.

CHEAP for (a). Moderate for (b), which needs a scope (a whole design? one increment? one component's subtree?) and a rendering.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (a) is not free — the local version works on string-id arcs while the foundation one needs a Graph built through GraphBuilder, so it trades forty lines of Kahn's for an impedance adapter, and the local one is already tested. (b) risks asserting a schedule reflow2 has no business asserting: a topological order is ONE valid order of many, and presenting it as THE order would be the same overreach dec:report-dont-judge exists to prevent. The honest output is probably the READY FRONTIER (what is unblocked) rather than a full ordering.

Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; the shape, especially frontier-vs-order, is open.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 answer "what order can this increment be built in, and what is buildable now?"
properties.rationale: Found by grepping reflow2 for any existing ordering concept and hitting a hand-rolled Kahn's in budget.rs — evidence both that the need is real and that the foundation function was not known to be there.
